docs.title: Project Overview
docs.text: GamerHouse is a multi-tenant Django REST Framework (DRF) backend for managing game libraries across multiple organizations. It provides a secure, scalable platform with role-based access control, email verification, and background task processing.

docs.title: Core Architecture
docs.text:
• Multi-tenancy – Complete data isolation between organizations
  • UUID primary keys – All models use UUIDs for security and scalability
  • Soft delete support with active/all object managers
  • Background tasks – Celery with Redis for async processing
  • Caching – Redis-backed Django cache with decorator-based response caching
  • Response filtering – Search and filter support for catalog endpoints
  • Rate limiting – Authentication endpoints protected with rate limiting (5/minute)

docs.title: Authentication & Authorization
docs.text:
• Email-based authentication – Login with email instead of username
  • Email verification – Required for new user registrations
  • OTP login flow – Two-step authentication with OTP verification
  • Password reset – Forgot password and reset password endpoints
  • JWT tokens – Using SimpleJWT with token blacklisting
  • Role-based access control – Super Admin, Admin, and Gamer roles

docs.title: Game Management
docs.text:
• Tenant-scoped games – Games are managed per tenant
  • Personal game library – Track your gaming progress
  • Status tracking – Wishlist, Playing, Completed, Dropped
  • Advanced filtering – Filter by status, platform, rating, hours played, genre
  • Game notes – Add personal notes to your games
  • Free tier limits – Max 5 games for free users

docs.title: Payments & Subscriptions
docs.text:
• Razorpay integration – Secure payment gateway integration
  • Premium subscriptions – Unlock unlimited game library entries
  • Subscription management – Track subscription status and billing
  • Payment verification – Secure signature verification for payments
  • Webhook handling – Automatic payment status updates via webhooks
  • Payment polling – Automatic reconciliation of pending payments

docs.title: Logging & Observability
docs.text:
• Structured JSON logging – JSON-formatted logs for easier parsing and analysis
  • Configurable logging – File, console, and log level configuration
  • Request/Response logging – Track all API requests and responses
  • Correlation IDs – Trace requests across distributed systems using context variables
  • Task logging – Background task execution tracking

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
• Standardized error responses – Consistent error format across all endpoints
  • Detailed error messages – Clear, actionable error descriptions
  • Proper HTTP status codes – Correct status codes for different error types
  • Middleware-based error handling – JSON error formatting and logging

docs.title: Multi-Tenancy
docs.text:
GamerHouse uses a shared database, shared schema multi-tenancy model where:

  • All data is scoped to a tenant via foreign keys
  • Users belong to a single tenant
  • Admins can only manage users and games within their tenant
  • Super admins can manage platform-wide resources
  • Automatic tenant context isolation – Tenant is automatically set during authentication and used for query filtering
  • Context variables – Tenant context is safely stored per request using Python's contextvars for async compatibility

docs.title: Role Hierarchy
docs.text:
1. Super Admin – Platform-level administration, manages catalog (games, genres, platforms), payments, and subscriptions
  2. Admin – Tenant-level administration, manages users and games within their tenant, handles premium subscriptions
  3. Gamer – Regular user, manages their own game library (limited to 5 games on free tier)

docs.title: Tech Stack
docs.text:
• Python 3.13+
  • Django 6.0
  • Django REST Framework 3.16+
  • PostgreSQL – Primary database
  • Redis – Caching and message broker
  • Celery – Background task processing
  • SimpleJWT – JWT authentication
  • django-filter – Advanced filtering
  • django-celery-beat – Periodic task scheduling
  • Razorpay SDK – Payment gateway integration

Key Architectural Decisions:

  • Multi-tenant shared database model with FK-based isolation
  • UUID primary keys across all models
  • Soft delete pattern with dual managers (objects, all_objects)
  • OTP-based login with email verification
  • JWT authentication with Redis-backed blacklisting
  • Celery for async tasks
  • DRF with custom renderers, pagination, and exception handling
  • Role-based access control (Super Admin, Admin, Gamer)

docs.title: Base Configuration
docs.text:
• Base URL: /api/v1/
  • API Versioning: URI-based (v1)
  • Authentication: JWT (Access & Refresh tokens)
  • Pagination:
    • Applied to all list endpoints
    • Default page size: 10
  • Update Strategy:
    • PATCH used for partial updates
    • PUT is not used

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
The API uses JWT (JSON Web Token) authentication. Include the access token in the Authorization header:

Authorization: Bearer <access_token>

docs.title: User Roles
docs.text:
• super_admin: Full system access
  • admin: Tenant administrator access
  • gamer: Regular user access

Purpose: Register a new gamer user for a specific tenant

Auth Required: No

Request Body: 

{

  "email": "string (email)",
  "password": "string",
  "confirm_password": "string"
}

docs.title: Registration & Email Verification
docs.text:
1. User submits username, email, password to POST /api/v1/auth/tenant/<tenant_id>/register/
    • Validations: Tenant exists, email/username unique, password strength
  2. User created with is_verified=False
  3. Email verification token generated and cached (60min TTL)
  4. Celery task sends verification email asynchronously
  5. User clicks link → GET /api/v1/auth/verify-email/?token=<token>
  6. Token validated, user marked as is_verified=True
  7. (Optional) User requests new link via POST /api/v1/auth/resend-verification/ (requires email)

docs.title: Login Flow (OTP-based)
docs.text:
1. User submits email and password to POST /api/v1/auth/login/
  2. Credentials validated; checks if user is active, verified, and tenant is active
  3. 6-digit OTP generated and hashed; hash stored in Redis (10min TTL)
  4. Celery task sends OTP via email
  5. User submits email and otp to POST /api/v1/auth/verify-login/
  6. OTP validated against cache (max 5 attempts)
  7. On success: OTP cache cleared, API issues Access Token (15min) and Refresh Token (1d)

docs.title: Token Management
docs.text:
1. Refresh: POST /api/v1/auth/refresh/ with refresh token
    • Rotates refresh token (issues new one, blacklists old one)
    • Checks if tenant is still active
  2. Logout: POST /api/v1/auth/logout/ with refresh token
    • Blacklists refresh token
    • Revokes access token via JTI blacklist
  3. Authentication: TenantJWTAuthentication validates token and ensures user/tenant are active

docs.title: Password Management
docs.text:
1. Forgot Password: POST /api/v1/auth/forgot-password/ with email
    • Generates reset token (30min TTL), caches it, and sends email link
  2. Reset Password: POST /api/v1/auth/reset-password/ with token, password, confirm_password
    • Validates token, updates password
    • Security: Revokes all existing sessions (blacklists all refresh tokens)
  3. Change Password: POST /api/v1/users/me/change-password/ (Authenticated)
    • Requires old_password and new_password
    • Updates password and revokes all other sessions

docs.title: Users Module
docs.text:
User

  • Custom user model based on AbstractUser
  • Fields:
  • email (Unique, Login Field)
  • username (Unique)
  • role (Enum: SUPER_ADMIN, ADMIN, GAMER, Default: GAMER)
  • tenant (FK → Tenant, Nullable)
  • is_verified (Boolean, Default: False)
  • is_active (Boolean, Default: True)
  • Key Logic:
  • Soft deletion support (overrides delete to set is_active=False and deleted_at)
  • Indexes on (tenant, role) and (email, is_verified)

docs.title: Tenants Module
docs.text:
Tenant

  • Represents the organization/account context
  • Fields:
  • name (Char)
  • status (Enum: ACTIVE, INACTIVE, PREMIUM, Default: ACTIVE)
  • Key Logic:
  • Central entity for multi-tenancy rules

docs.title: Tenant Games Module
docs.text:
TenantGame

  • Links a Tenant to a Catalog Game (Availability)
  • Fields:
  • tenant (FK → Tenant)
  • game (FK → Catalog Game)
  • Key Logic:
  • Unique constraint on (tenant, game) (where active) implies a tenant cannot have duplicate entries for the same game.
  • Soft deletion support.

docs.title: Games Module (Catalog)
docs.text:
Game

  • Represents a global/catalog game entry
  • Fields:
  • title (Char)
  • description (Text, Optional)
  • release_date (Date, Optional)
  • genre (FK → Genre)
  • platforms (M2M → Platform)

docs.title: Genres Module
docs.text:
Genre

  • Reference data for categorizing games
  • Fields:
  • name (Char)

docs.title: Platforms Module
docs.text:
Platform

  • Reference data for gaming platforms
  • Fields:
  • name (Char)

docs.title: User Games Module
docs.text:
UserGame

  • Represents a specific user's instance/progress of a game
  • Fields:
  • user (FK → User)
  • tenant_game (FK → TenantGame)
  • platform (FK → Platform)
  • status (Enum: WISHLIST, PLAYING, COMPLETED, DROPPED, Default: WISHLIST)
  • tenant (FK → Tenant)
  • hours_played (PositiveInt, Optional)
  • personal_rating (PositiveSmallInt, Optional)
  • started_on (Date, Optional)
  • completed_on (Date, Optional)
  • Key Logic:
  • Indexes on (user, status), created_at, (user, tenant).

UserGameNote

  • Notes attached to a user game
  • Fields:
  • user_game (FK → UserGame)
  • note (Text)
  • tenant (FK → Tenant)

docs.title: Payments Module
docs.text:
Payment

  • Tracks individual payment transactions via Razorpay
  • Fields:
  • tenant (FK → Tenant)
  • admin (FK → User)
  • razorpay_order_id (Char, Unique)
  • razorpay_payment_id (Char, Nullable)
  • razorpay_signature (Char, Nullable)
  • amount (Int, in paise)
  • status (Enum: CREATED, AUTHORIZED, PAID, VERIFIED, ACTIVATED, FAILED, REFUNDED, CANCELLED)
  • verified_at (DateTime, Optional)
  • activated_at (DateTime, Optional)
  • error_message (Text, Optional)
  • metadata (JSON)
  • Key Logic:
  • State transitions validation.

Subscription

  • Tracks tenant subscription status
  • Fields:
  • tenant (OneToOne → Tenant)
  • payment (FK → Payment, Nullable, tracks activation payment)
  • status (Enum: NONE, PENDING, ACTIVE, EXPIRED, Default: NONE)
  • activated_at (DateTime, Optional)
  • deactivated_at (DateTime, Optional)
  • Key Logic:
  • Designed for lifetime activation (One subscription per tenant).

WebhookEvent

  • Logs raw webhook requests for audit
  • Fields:
  • event_id (Char, Unique)
  • event_type (Char)
  • payload (JSON)
  • raw_body (Text)
  • status (Enum: PENDING, PROCESSING, PROCESSED, FAILED, Default: PENDING)
  • error_message (Text, Optional)
  • retry_count (Int)
  • processed_at (DateTime, Optional)

docs.title: Key Design Principles
docs.text:
• Normalization: Catalog data (Game, Genre, Platform) is separated from Tenant and User data.
  • Multi-tenancy: Almost all interaction models (User, UserGame, Payment, TenantGame) link explicitly to Tenant.
  • Soft Deletion: Core models inherit from BaseModel which likely provides deleted_at.
  • Enums: Used strictly for Statuses and Roles to enforce business logic.

docs.title: Uniqueness:
docs.text:
• users.email
  • users.username
  • tenant_games(tenant, game) (Active records)
  • payments.razorpay_order_id
  • webhook_events.event_id

docs.title: Performance Indexes:
docs.text:
• users(tenant, role)
  • user_games(user, status)
  • payments(tenant, status)
  • webhook_events(status, created_at)

docs.title: Roles
docs.text: The system uses a Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) system with three distinct roles.

docs.title: 1. Super Admin
docs.text:
Scope: Platform-wide administration.

Key Capabilities:

  • Tenant Management: Full control (Create, Read, Update, Delete) over all tenants.
  • User Management: Can manage Admin users across the system.
  • Catalog Management: Exclusive rights to create, update, and delete global resources including Genres, Platforms, and the Global Game Catalog.
  • System Access: Unrestricted access to most system resources, with the exception of private user data (e.g., User Games) where explicit access is not required.

docs.title: 2. Admin (Tenant Admin)
docs.text:
Scope: Tenant-level administration.

Key Capabilities:

  • Tenant Management: Read-only access to their own tenant's details. Cannot see other tenants.
  • User Management: Full control over users (Gamers) within their own tenant. Cannot manage Super Admins or themselves via the User API.
  • Tenant Games: Full control to add or manage games specific to their tenant.
  • Catalog Access: Read-only access to the Global Game Catalog, Genres, and Platforms.
  • User Games: Can view and manage game lists for users within their tenant.

docs.title: 3. Gamer
docs.text:
Scope: Personal user data.

Key Capabilities:

  • Self Management: Can manage their own profile and password.
  • User Games: Full control (Create, Read, Update, Delete) over their own personal game list.
  • Tenant Games: Read-only access to games available in their tenant.
  • Catalog Access: Read-only access to Genres and Platforms. No access to the raw Global Game Catalog.
  • Restrictions: Strictly isolated from other users' data and administrative functions.
